<a id="architecture"></a>

## Architecture

Rust only. u1: Omp|Pi route directly to the queue-backed Observe/message.pushed stream before Transport, composer gates, and select_rung. u2 (ruling 2026-09-02): the actual drain is crates/daemon/src/pointer/worker.rs; add config thresholds, a dedicated per-sender queued-notice queue, additive /v1/notices read-and-ack in daemon/http, and cli/client + main stderr rendering. Notices never enter or compete with the user inbox; no envelope version bump. u3: pane tap bytes are rendered output, never keystrokes; a fresh recognized composer box is authoritative. Blank permits; non-blank returns human-typing with the first 12 hex of SHA-256 in additive draft_sha fields on InjectionVerdict, StagedSubmission, and DeliveryOutcome::Queued.

<a id="isolation"></a>

## Isolation

| Field | Value |
| --- | --- |
| mode | solo-pm in the plan worktree |
| note | Default: each coder gets its own worktree, branching off the PM's plan branch; unit lands back onto the plan branch (PM merges — coders never merge). Shared-tree work is the retro-proven #1 hazard (staged sweeps, untrustworthy greens) — only choose it for trivially disjoint single-wave work, and then file-scoped `git add` only, never -A. REMEMBER: fences partition WRITE intent, not the build — a mid-refactor sibling can still break your compile, so waves must respect build dependencies, and a broken workspace build is a PM composition concern, not a coder's to fix cross-fence. |
